overseasStockTax.title: Overseas Stock Tax Calculator
overseasStockTax.subtitle: Work out Korean capital gains tax (22% including local tax) on the foreign stocks you sold in 2026, and see how much a year-end loss sale or filling the ₩2.5M deduction could save.

rows.title: Gains and losses by stock
rows.hint: Enter the KRW buy amount and sell amount (market value for stocks you still hold) shown in your brokerage app. Sold stocks set this year's tax; held stocks are used for the year-end tax-saving plan.
rows.name: Stock {n} name

fee.label: Trading fee rate
fee.hint: Buy and sell fees are deductible expenses. 0.25% is a typical online rate for foreign stocks; promotional rates vary by broker.

result.label: Overseas stock tax due this year
result.note: Covers trades settled 1 Jan–31 Dec 2026; amounts under 1 KRW are cut. The return converts each buy and sell at the base exchange rate on its settlement date, so figures may differ slightly from your app. Gains on taxable Korean shares (major-shareholder or unlisted) are netted in too.

status.loss: Your stocks sold this year net to zero or a loss, so no tax is due. Unused losses do not carry over to next year.
status.within: You are within the ₩2.5M basic deduction, so no tax is due. You can realize another {left} KRW of gains tax-free.

share.label: Overseas stock gains sold this year: {realizedM}M KRW
share.headline: Overseas stock tax: {tax} KRW
share.subRoom: {room} KRW more can be realized tax-free
share.text: With {realizedM}M KRW of overseas stock gains sold this year, the capital gains tax (incl. local tax) is {tax} KRW.

loss.title: Sell losers to offset gains
loss.desc: All overseas stock gains and losses settled in the same year are netted. Selling a losing position so it settles this year offsets your gains and cuts the tax.
loss.noNeed: Your realized gains are within the ₩2.5M deduction, so there is no need to realize losses. See "Fill the ₩2.5M deduction".
loss.noLoss: You have no losing positions. Add a losing stock as "Still held" to see how much to sell.
loss.result: Selling your losing positions cuts the tax from {before} KRW to {after} KRW, saving {saving} KRW.
loss.short: Even after realizing every loss, {left} KRW of gains stays above the deduction.
loss.note: Losses do not carry over, so realize only enough to bring your gains down to ₩2.5M. You can buy back and keep the stock, but the lower cost basis means a bigger gain when you sell later. Weigh fees and FX costs too.

fill.title: Fill the ₩2.5M deduction
fill.desc: The ₩2.5M basic deduction is lost if unused. Selling winners up to the unused amount and buying them back raises your cost basis tax-free.
fill.noRoom: Your realized gains already exceed ₩2.5M, so no deduction is left to fill.
fill.noGain: You can realize {room} KRW of gains tax-free, but you have no winning positions. Add a winning stock as "Still held".
fill.result: You can realize up to {room} KRW of gains tax-free. Selling and buying back the amounts below locks in {filled} KRW of tax-free gain and can cut future tax by up to {future} KRW.
fill.itemAll: Sell all ({sell} KRW) and buy back → {gain} KRW gain
fill.itemPart: Sell about {sell} KRW and buy back → {gain} KRW gain
fill.fees: Fees for selling and buying back: about {fees} KRW (FX costs and price moves not included)
fill.note: "Up to" assumes that gain would otherwise be realized in a later year when you are above ₩2.5M. Prices can move between the sale and the buy-back, and the actual gain uses the settlement-date exchange rate.

compare.title: Tax by scenario
compare.note: Held stocks are assumed sold at today's market value, net of buy and sell fees. Tax includes local income tax.

deadline.title: To count in this year
deadline.text: The sale date is the settlement date, not the trade date. US stocks settle one business day after the trade (T+1), so a sale must settle by 31 December to count in 2026. The last trading day and cut-off time vary by broker, so check your broker's December notice and leave a margin.

filing.title: File and pay: May 2027
filing.text: Overseas stocks need no interim return: file and pay between 1 and 31 May of the following year (online via Hometax). Local income tax (10% of the capital gains tax) is filed and paid on Wetax right after the Hometax return. Missing the deadline adds penalties for non-filing and late payment.

agent.title: Broker filing service
agent.text: Many brokers take applications around March–April and file the overseas stock tax return for you (often free; dates and terms vary). If you use several brokers, all gains and losses must be combined into one return with a single ₩2.5M deduction.

rules.title: Overseas stock tax rules at a glance

rows.v: Shares of foreign companies and shares listed on foreign exchanges (including corporate-type funds). Foreign-investing ETFs listed in Korea are not covered by this tax.
20% of the taxable amount + 2% local income tax = 22%. Shares of Korean SMEs listed abroad: 10%.
₩2.5M per person per year, applied once across taxable Korean shares and all brokers.

All overseas stock gains and losses settled in the same year are combined, together with Korean major-shareholder listed shares and unlisted shares. Korean listed shares sold on-exchange by minority shareholders are not taxable and are not netted. Unused losses do not carry over.
Sale proceeds use the base or arbitrage rate on the day they are paid in; purchase cost and fees use the rate on the day they are paid out (each settlement date).
Buy and sell fees and other costs paid directly for the sale are deducted. Tax paid abroad is credited as foreign tax or deducted as an expense.
If you bought the same stock several times, the earliest shares are treated as sold first (FIFO). Moving-average figures applied consistently by your broker are also accepted.
No interim return; file between 1 and 31 May of the following year. Trades settled in 2026 are due by 31 May 2027.

tips.title: Good to know
items: Even if the share price is flat, a stronger dollar than when you bought creates a KRW gain that can be taxed. Likewise a dollar gain can be a KRW loss if the dollar weakens.
Brokers compute cost basis differently (FIFO or moving average), so the same trades can show different gains. Get your broker's capital gains statement before filing.

If you sell shares received as a gift from a spouse, parent or child within one year, the gain is computed from the giver's purchase price (Income Tax Act Art. 97-2). To step up the basis by gifting, the recipient must wait more than a year before selling.
If a family member's overseas stock gain (before the basic deduction) exceeds ₩1M in a year, you cannot claim them as a dependant in that year's year-end settlement (Income Tax Act Art. 50).

For foreign shares held since before 23 Dec 2025 and sold in 2026 through a Domestic Market Return Account (RIA) whose money stays in for a year, sales from August onward can deduct up to 50% of the gain (Restriction of Special Taxation Act Art. 91-26, ₩50M deposit limit). This calculator does not apply it — ask your broker.
Dividends from overseas stocks are dividend income, not capital gains, and are taxed separately from this calculation.
